items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1979-03-26
items.q: I think Dutch was playing a lot with Frank when I first met him. Dutch Andrews, uh. Mm-hmm. And, uh, Burton. But he was just, anybody he could get, he would book dates and he'd organize the bands and strictly non-union.

ctx.x: Think of how many phone calls a Lita would have to make, how many telegrams he'd have to send. And the expenses must have just been, well, of course it was cheap then, but it was a terrible thing for a Lita to have to do out of making ten dollars on a job.

Yeah. But you must remember that the money was so very scarce. And I played many jobs throughout East Texas and southern Louisiana where we'd be playing for an American Legion dance or an Elf's Club or something like that where we didn't have a guarantee that it would be a subscription dance and sometimes we'd make three bucks, sometimes we'd make seven bucks, sometimes we didn't make anything. Of course they were generally booked on a seven to thirty basis. And so, to kind of get back to New Orleans, I remember…

I don't recall the name really, but I probably have heard it because it sounds vaguely familiar. Yeah, I suspect he's long since dead. Well, I've heard too many names anyway. Yeah. Well, that's right. Yeah, you, you know, people like you and I were constantly working with names. You just can't remember everybody. Right. And, uh, anyway, uh, I hate to keep coming back to the same people, but we never did get to Dick Coleman. Excuse me.
